CVE-2026-66295.title: Processing instruction target and content emitted unescaped in Saxy encoder allows XML injection
CVE-2026-66295.description:
Saxy's XML encoder writes the target and the content of a processing instruction into the output document verbatim, without validation or escaping. The encoder builds the construct by concatenating both fields between <? and ?>, so neither field is checked against the constraints the XML specification places on it.

Because ?> terminates a processing instruction, a target or content value containing that sequence closes the construct at a position the attacker chooses. Everything the attacker writes after it is emitted as ordinary markup at document level, which allows arbitrary elements, attributes, and further processing instructions to be injected into the serialized document. Appending a matching <? keeps the encoder's own terminator well-formed, so the result still parses and the injection is silent rather than a visible corruption. static void sata_fsl_host_stop(struct ata_host *host)
{

iounmap(host_priv->hcr_base);

started.

and host_priv as well, and it is reachable from the two

CVE-2026-99680.title: xfs: mark the inode preallocated for pNFS write layouts past EOF
CVE-2026-99680.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: mark the inode preallocated for pNFS write layouts past EOF

xfs_fs_map_blocks() marks the inode XFS_DIFLAG_PREALLOC only when it
allocates blocks for a write layout. A write layout past EOF can also
hand out allocated blocks, such as speculative preallocation. blockgc
then frees them under the layout, and another file may get them.

Mark the inode whenever a write mapping ends past EOF.

CVE-2026-99734.title: mm/shmem: make shmem_file() check the file's inode
CVE-2026-99734.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/shmem: make shmem_file() check the file's inode

shmem_file() only checks if file->f_mapping is a shmem mapping. This
mapping can belong to another file, however, as with a Coda file backed
by a tmpfs container after mmap().

So it does not guarantee that the file inode is an actual shmem inode.

Seal handling and memfd preservation use this check before accessing
shmem inode state, so they can access an inode of the wrong type.

Let's make shmem_file() check the inode's file operations instead, to
identify shmem inodes reliably. This will identify regular shmem inodes,
including memfds and ordinary tmpfs files, independently of wrapper file
operations.

Use shmem_mapping() in collapse_file() instead to not change the behavior
of collapse_file(): it operates on the page cache and uses mapping->host
for shmem inode operations. Focusing on the file does not seem relevant.

CVE-2026-99789.title: block: restore the iterator when rejecting a misaligned bio
CVE-2026-99789.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

block: restore the iterator when rejecting a misaligned bio

bio_iov_iter_get_pages() can extract some iovecs before encountering a
misaligned one. It releases the pages and rejects the entire bio, but
leaves the supplied iterator advanced.

An iomap direct-I/O caller may subsequently reexpand the iterator's
byte count and fall back to buffered I/O. The reexpanded count then
includes bytes before the iterator's current segment, potentially
causing iterate_iovec() to read beyond the imported iovec array.

In a reproducer using an initial empty iovec followed by 10-byte and
1015-byte segments, writev() returned 1015 instead of 1025 and KASAN
reported an 8-byte read beyond the nine-element iovec allocation.
Saving and restoring the iterator on the rejected-bio path makes
writev() return 1025 and eliminates the KASAN report.
